qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Ofcom regulatory price caps on Openreach wholesale broadband access, combined with aggressive altnet fiber overbuilding (CityFibre, Hyperoptic) and ongoing legacy copper line losses, compress returns. GAAP ROIC of 6–7% and ROCE of 8.3–8.5% fall far short of the 12% hurdle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & regulated wholesale price caps, REJECT). Openreach represents critical national UK infrastructure, but Ofcom price controls and fierce altnet fiber competition structurally suppress returns on invested capital to 6–7% (ROCE 8.3–8.5%). Heavy multi-billion FTTP capex, £19B+ net debt, and pension obligations leave zero pricing power above inflation.
qualitative.evidence: BT Group reported ROCE of 8.3% (FY23) and 8.5% (FY24), with independent ROIC estimated at ~6-7%, failing the 12% Munger threshold. FTTP buildout to 25 million homes consumes £5B+ in annual capex while Openreach faces net broadband line losses to competitive altnets. Regulated wholesale access formulas prevent real above-inflation pricing.
